paragraphs: Use these sheets anywhere December practice happens: morning tubs, early-finisher folders, a calm table activity during party week, or a take-home packet for the holiday break. Because every worksheet pairs a printable PDF with a playable online version, the same Christmas exercise works on paper at school and on a tablet at grandma's house.

The set leans on pictures rather than text, so it fits mixed-language classrooms well — a child can count ornaments or match gifts before they can read English instructions. Answer keys are included with every PDF, and nothing here requires an account or a subscription.

These Easter worksheets are built for the weeks around spring break: eggs, bunnies, and spring friends carry counting, early addition, sorting, patterning, and letter work, so the holiday excitement points at practice instead of away from it. Print the PDF with its answer key, or let children play the same exercise online with instant feedback.
Everything is picture-first, which keeps the sheets friendly for early readers and multilingual classrooms, and every download here is free — no account, no limits.

Winter worksheets cover the long stretch from December to February: snowmen, mittens, and cozy winter friends carry counting, addition, sorting, patterns, matching, and word work. They make easy sub-plan filler, indoor-recess work, and January review packets after the holiday reset.

Unlike Christmas-specific pages, these sheets stay useful all season and work in any classroom regardless of what children celebrate. Each one prints as a free PDF with an answer key, or plays online with no signup.

Spring worksheets put flowers, bugs, rain boots, and garden friends to work on counting, early addition, sorting, patterning, matching, and letter practice — a natural fit for the March-to-May stretch when classrooms turn to growth, weather, and life-cycle themes.

The pictures do the heavy lifting, so the sheets suit early readers and multilingual groups alike. Every worksheet is a free printable PDF with an answer key, and every one can also be played online with instant checking — no account needed.

Summer worksheets are made for two moments: the wind-down weeks at the end of the school year, and the long break itself. Beach days, ice cream, and sunny friends carry counting, addition, sorting, patterns, matching, and word work — an easy way to keep skills warm without turning July into school.

Parents can print a small packet for road trips or quiet mornings, or hand over a tablet for the online version of the same exercise. Every sheet is free, comes with an answer key, and needs no account.

These 4th of July worksheets bring flags, fireworks, and summer-party pictures to counting, addition, sorting, patterns, matching, and word work — a fun anchor for the holiday week in summer programs, camps, and at home.

The set spans preschool through early elementary, so one download covers siblings at different stages. Every worksheet is a free printable PDF with an answer key, and each one plays online too — no account required.

Thanksgiving worksheets dress November practice in harvest pictures: turkeys, pumpkins, and autumn friends carry counting, early addition, sorting, and word work for the short, busy weeks before the break.
They print as free PDFs with answer keys and play online with instant feedback, so the same sheet works for the classroom table and the kids' corner at the family gathering. No account, no cost.
